title: Elimination of Bacteria from Microalgal Culture Using Antibiotics
author: Adriana Lopes dos Santos
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.be9wjh7e

steps.title: Prepare antibiotic stock solution
steps.instruction: Wearing appropriate protective clothing, mix 20 mL of pure water with the following antibiotics to obtain a 10× stock: Cefotaxime 5 g L⁻¹, Carbenicillin 5 g L⁻¹, Kanamycin 2 g L⁻¹, Augmentin 2 g L⁻¹. Filter‑sterilize the solution through a 0.1 µm or 0.22 µm filter into a sterile bottle. Store the bottle refrigerated (up to several weeks) or aliquot and keep at –20 °C.

steps.title: Harvest and resuspend algae cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 20 mL of a healthy, log‑phase micro‑algal culture (speed and time depend on species; e.g., 1600 g for 2 min for *E. hux*). Optionally check the supernatant for bacterial contaminants by flow cytometry before proceeding. Resuspend the pellet in fresh sterile media that has been filter‑sterilized (0.1 µm or 0.22 µm). Adjust the resuspension volume to obtain a dense inoculum, typically 600 µL of sterile media (volume may be altered as needed).

steps.title: Set up antibiotic treatment tubes
steps.instruction:
Prepare six treatment tubes with the following composition (all volumes in µL):
1. 10 % antibiotic: 40 µL 10× antibiotic mix, 100 µL algae cells, 1860 µL algae media, 2 µL enriched media (LB or SOC).
2. 15 % antibiotic: 60 µL 10× antibiotic mix, 100 µL algae cells, 1840 µL algae media, 2 µL enriched media.
3. 20 % antibiotic: 80 µL 10× antibiotic mix, 100 µL algae cells, 1820 µL algae media, 2 µL enriched media.
4. 25 % antibiotic: 100 µL 10× antibiotic mix, 100 µL algae cells, 1800 µL algae media, 2 µL enriched media.
5. 35 % antibiotic: 140 µL 10× antibiotic mix, 100 µL algae cells, 1760 µL algae media, 2 µL enriched media.
6. 50 % antibiotic: 200 µL 10× antibiotic mix, 100 µL algae cells, 1700 µL algae media, 2 µL enriched media.
Gently vortex each tube to ensure thorough mixing.

steps.title: Incubate treatment tubes
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in an illuminated incubator set to the optimum growth temperature for the algal strain.

steps.title: Sample and inoculate into 24‑well plate
steps.instruction: At each of the following incubation times – 16 h, 24 h, 48 h, 72 h, and 80 h – withdraw approximately 10 µL from every treatment tube and inoculate it into 1 mL of fresh growth medium contained in a well of a 24‑well plate.

steps.title: Incubate plate
steps.instruction: Incubate the 24‑well plate at the same optimum temperature and illumination conditions as the tubes.

steps.title: Monitor growth and contamination
steps.instruction: Over the following week, assess algal growth and the presence of bacterial contaminants in each well using a flow cytometer.

steps.title: Transfer axenic cultures to fresh media
steps.instruction: Move any wells that show axenic (bacteria‑free) algae into 15 mL of freshly sterilized growth medium, even if multiple wells belong to the same strain.

steps.title: Cryopreserve and prepare for sequencing
steps.instruction: If possible, cryopreserve the axenic strain immediately. For genome‑sequencing purposes, once axenicity is confirmed, scale up to 1–2 L of dense culture, harvest cells by centrifugation, and freeze the cell pellet at –80 °C for later DNA extraction.

steps.title: Repeat treatment cycles
steps.instruction: Repeat the antibiotic‑treatment (step 3) and incubation (step 4) cycles 5–6 times, optimizing the wash step for each algal group. Use flow cytometry after each cycle to balance cell recovery against bacterial removal efficiency.
